spans.s:
Pṛkṣa (literally, perhaps ‘swift’) is the proper name of a man in an obscure verse of the Rigveda.
Foot notes ii. 13, 8. Cf. Pischel, Vedische Studien, 1, 97.

Pṛkṣa-yāma occurs once in the plural in the Rigveda. Roth suggests the sense of ‘faring with swift steeds,’ and thinks a proper name is meant. Pischel holds that the word is an epithet of the Pajras, and that it means ‘performing splendid sacrifices.’
Foot notes i. 122, 7.
St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v.
Vedische Studien, 1, 97, 98.
